verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Lean has exactly the C_Q = C_N = 0 branch: `angularLag` is ∫₀^X H S_q dx / (X H(X,η)) and `axialLag` is ∫₀^X S_n dx / X, with `primitive` the integral from 0 to X, i.e. the display with the constants dropped. The constant-carrying family — and with it the statement that every solution of (4.9) has this form, which is what the display asserts — was not found as a declaration. It is a short argument away: `angular_lag_primitive_iff` / `axial_lag_primitive_iff` turn each row of (4.9) into the exactness of (X H Q_s)' = H S_q and (X N_s)' = S_n, and the fundamental theorem of calculus then gives the general solution with an η-dependent constant. Rated low because the paper itself keeps only the C = 0 branch (the constants are killed in the next display by regularity at X = 0), so the branch Lean fixes is the branch the paper uses; what is missing is the uniqueness half.
